newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworkers talks to resume on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworkers talks to resume on Wednesday.

text.p: Talks between engineering and metalworkers unions and employers will resume on Wednesday after a second day of meetings that was judged positive by Labour Minister Tiziano Treu.
"Participants said today's session was positive and we will have another session tomorrow," Treu told reporters after the two-hour meeting. "We'll do everything to end this matter quickly."
Talks resumed on Monday for the first time in more than a month to try to end a pay dispute which involves some 1.7 million workers. The sector's two-year contract expired in June.
The government suggested in December that management give workers an average 200,000 lire ($124) per month pay increase.
Unions, which had been seeking a 230,000 lire ($142) increase, accepted the proposals but the main industry group Federmeccanica rejected it claiming it fueled inflation.

Italian media have widely reported that Federmeccanica was ready to offer a 180,000 lire ($111) per month pay increase but wanted the contract period to be extended to 30 months from the standard two years.
The unions in the industry, FIOM, FIM and UILM, announced on Tuesday a three-hour strike to take place by Friday to press Federmeccanica to accept the government's proposal.

FIOM leader Claudio Damiani said on Monday that it would never agree to a 30-month contract because this was a misinterpretation of a landmark 1993 accord on labour costs between the labour confederations, Confindustria and the government that ended a system of automatic inflation-linked wage increases.
"A longer contract would modify the content of the accord, and we would never agree to that," he said.
